questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.1 Bank feeds — supported file formats for manual upload
questions.keyword: .CSV .QFX .QBO .OFX supported file formats
questions.text: Which file formats can be used to manually upload bank transactions to QuickBooks Online when a financial institution does not support automatic bank feeds?

answers.text: .CSV, .QFX, .QBO, and .OFX
.XLS, .CSV, .PDF, and .QBO
.QFX, .OFX, .PDF, and .XML
.CSV, .TXT, .JSON, and .QBO

explanations.a: The Student Guide states QBO supports manual transaction uploads in .CSV, .QFX, .QBO, and .OFX file formats.
explanations.b: .XLS and .PDF are not supported upload formats for QBO bank transactions; .PDF cannot be parsed as transaction data.
explanations.c: .PDF and .XML are not listed as supported upload formats in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: .TXT and .JSON are not supported upload formats for QBO bank transactions as described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: For Review Reviewed Excluded three Banking Center tabs
questions.text: The Banking Center in QuickBooks Online has three main tabs for managing downloaded transactions. Which set correctly names all three?

answers.text: Transactions, Cleared, Matched.
For Review, Reviewed, Excluded.
Pending, Accepted, Rejected.
Downloaded, Posted, Archived.

explanations.a: Transactions, Cleared, and Matched are not the names of the Banking Center tabs described in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: The Student Guide identifies the three Banking Center tabs as For Review (transactions awaiting action), Reviewed (accepted/matched transactions), and Excluded (transactions removed from consideration).
explanations.c: Pending, Accepted, and Rejected are not the Banking Center tab names used in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Downloaded, Posted, and Archived are not the Banking Center tab names described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: For Review All Recognized sub-tabs
questions.text: The For Review tab in the Banking Center contains two sub-tabs. What are they?

answers.text: Matched and Unmatched.
Downloaded and Categorized.
All and Recognized.
New and Existing.

explanations.a: Matched and Unmatched are not the sub-tab names described in the Student Guide for the For Review tab.
explanations.b: Downloaded and Categorized are not the For Review sub-tab names in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: The Student Guide identifies the two sub-tabs within For Review as All (every downloaded transaction awaiting action) and Recognized (transactions that QBO has already identified a likely category or match for).
explanations.d: New and Existing are not the For Review sub-tab names described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: reconciliation gear icon Accounting Reconcile left navigation
questions.text: How does a bookkeeper access the Reconcile feature in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: +New → Other → Reconcile.
Reports tab → Reconciliation Summary → Start Reconciliation.
Banking Center → Reviewed tab → Reconcile button at the top right.
Gear icon → Accounting → Reconcile, or left navigation bar → Accounting → Reconcile.

explanations.a: +New opens transaction creation screens; Reconcile is not listed under Other in the +New menu.
explanations.b: The Reports tab leads to the Report Center; starting reconciliation is not initiated from a report.
explanations.c: The Reviewed tab shows previously accepted transactions; there is no Reconcile button on that tab.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states Reconcile is found under the gear icon → Accounting, or by clicking Accounting in the left navigation bar and selecting Reconcile.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: Difference zero reconciliation finalized Finish now
questions.text: When completing a bank reconciliation in QuickBooks Online, what must be true before the reconciliation can be finalized by clicking Finish now?

answers.text: The Difference amount shown on the reconciliation screen must equal $0.00.
All transactions in the For Review tab must be cleared before the reconciliation begins.
Every downloaded bank transaction must be individually matched to a QBO transaction.
The bank statement must be uploaded as a PDF attachment before Finish now becomes available.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states the Difference — calculated as the cleared balance minus the statement ending balance — must equal $0.00 before the reconciliation can be completed with Finish now.
explanations.b: Bank feed review and reconciliation are separate processes; For Review transactions do not need to be fully cleared before starting reconciliation.
explanations.c: Transactions can be cleared in QBO from manual entry without bank feed matching; complete matching of every downloaded transaction is not required to reconcile.
explanations.d: No PDF upload of the bank statement is required to complete reconciliation in QBO.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: green 1 record found match indicator existing transaction
questions.text: In the For Review tab of the Banking Center, a downloaded transaction displays a green match indicator reading '1 record found.' What does this mean?

answers.text: The transaction was already manually entered in QBO by the bookkeeper and is awaiting confirmation.
QBO found exactly one existing QBO transaction that is a likely match for this downloaded entry.
The transaction was accepted by a bank rule and has already been posted automatically.
The bank download file contained only one transaction from this bank account in this session.

explanations.a: A green '1 record found' indicator means QBO has identified a potential match; it does not confirm the bookkeeper has manually entered the transaction.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states a green '1 record found' indicator means QBO has found exactly one existing transaction in QBO that is a likely match for the downloaded bank entry.
explanations.c: A bank rule acceptance would move the transaction directly to Reviewed; a green match indicator means the bookkeeper still needs to confirm the match.
explanations.d: The number in the indicator reflects potential matching records in QBO, not the total number of downloaded bank transactions.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: bank rules categorize automatically future downloaded transactions
questions.text: What is the purpose of creating bank rules in the QuickBooks Online Banking Center?

answers.text: To prevent certain bank transactions from ever appearing in the For Review tab.
To automatically upload transactions from the bank to QBO on a user-defined schedule.
To automatically categorize or match future downloaded transactions based on conditions defined by the bookkeeper.
To lock accepted transactions in the Reviewed tab so they cannot be accidentally undone.

explanations.a: Bank rules do not block transactions from downloading; they categorize transactions after they arrive in For Review.
explanations.b: Bank feed scheduling and connectivity are handled separately from bank rules; rules act on transactions after they are downloaded.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states bank rules allow bookkeepers to define conditions (such as transaction description or bank text) and actions (such as a payee and account assignment) that QBO applies automatically to future downloaded transactions meeting those conditions.
explanations.d: Bank rules do not lock Reviewed transactions; undoing an accepted transaction is done from the Reviewed tab separately.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: Reviewed tab accepted matched transactions bank feed
questions.text: After a bookkeeper accepts or matches a downloaded transaction in the For Review tab, where does that transaction move in the Banking Center?

answers.text: It moves to the Cleared tab, where it awaits the monthly reconciliation.
It is posted to the Chart of Accounts with no further tracking in the Banking Center.
It moves to the Excluded tab until the monthly reconciliation is completed.
It moves to the Reviewed tab, which holds all accepted and matched transactions from the bank feed.

explanations.a: There is no Cleared tab in the Banking Center; the three tabs are For Review, Reviewed, and Excluded.
explanations.b: While the transaction is posted to QBO accounts, it is also visible in the Reviewed tab for reference and potential undo.
explanations.c: The Excluded tab is for transactions intentionally removed from consideration, not for accepted transactions awaiting reconciliation.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states accepted and matched transactions move to the Reviewed tab in the Banking Center, where they remain accessible for reference or undo.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: Add action new transaction category payee For Review
questions.text: A downloaded bank transaction has no matching QBO transaction and represents a brand-new expense. What is the correct action in the For Review tab?

answers.text: Click Add on the transaction row, assign the appropriate account and payee, and save to post the transaction to QBO.
Click Match and select the nearest QBO transaction even if amounts differ slightly.
Move the transaction to the Excluded tab so it does not affect the books.
Click Batch and use the batch action to auto-code all unmatched transactions at once.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states that for new transactions without a QBO record, the bookkeeper should click Add, assign the appropriate account, payee, and any other details, then save to create the transaction in QBO.
explanations.b: Matching a downloaded transaction to an existing QBO transaction that has a different amount would create an inaccurate record; Add is the correct action for genuinely new transactions.
explanations.c: Excluding a legitimate new business expense means it will not post to the books; expenses that belong in the company records should be added, not excluded.
explanations.d: Batch actions exist for processing multiple transactions but clicking Add individually is the correct process for carefully categorizing new transactions.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.5 Actions — Match for existing QBO transactions
questions.keyword: Match existing QBO transaction confirm cleared check number
questions.text: A downloaded bank transaction carries a check number that matches a check already entered manually in QuickBooks Online. What action should the bookkeeper take in the For Review tab?

answers.text: Click Add to create a new separate record alongside the existing QBO check.
Click Match to link the downloaded transaction to the existing QBO check, confirming the check has cleared the bank.
Click Exclude to remove the bank transaction since the QBO check already exists.
Delete the manually entered QBO check and let the bank feed version become the authoritative record.

explanations.a: Clicking Add when a matching QBO transaction already exists would create a duplicate transaction and overstate expenses.
explanations.b: The Student Guide instructs bookkeepers to click Match when a downloaded transaction corresponds to an existing QBO record, linking the two and confirming the transaction has cleared the bank.
explanations.c: Excluding the downloaded transaction would leave the manually entered check unconfirmed and unmatch it from the bank feed, complicating reconciliation.
explanations.d: Deleting manually entered transactions disrupts the audit trail; the Match action properly links the existing entry to the downloaded bank transaction.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: split transaction two categories expand For Review row
questions.text: A $500 downloaded credit card charge covers two different expense categories. How is this handled within the Banking Center For Review tab?

answers.text: The bookkeeper must split the download file manually into two transactions and re-upload the corrected file.
The transaction cannot be split in QBO; it must be entered as a single expense and adjusted with a journal entry later.
Within the For Review transaction row, the bookkeeper expands the transaction and splits it across two or more categories that together total $500.
The bookkeeper accepts the transaction as one expense then creates a second expense to correct the allocation.

explanations.a: There is no need to modify the download file; QBO's split transaction feature handles multi-category charges within the Banking Center.
explanations.b: The Student Guide describes a built-in split feature for downloaded transactions; a separate journal entry adjustment is unnecessary.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that from the For Review tab, a transaction can be expanded and split across multiple account categories, with the amounts for each category entered so they total the full transaction amount.
explanations.d: Accepting a full transaction to one account and then creating a second separate transaction to adjust it creates unnecessary additional records; the split feature handles this in one step.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.11 Reconciliation — statement ending balance and date entry
questions.keyword: statement ending balance ending date reconciliation start
questions.text: When beginning a bank reconciliation in QuickBooks Online, which two pieces of information from the bank statement must be entered into the opening reconciliation screen?

answers.text: The starting balance and the number of transactions on the statement.
The routing number and account number to verify which account is being reconciled.
The previous reconciliation date and the statement period length in days.
The statement ending balance and the statement ending date.

explanations.a: The number of transactions is not required as an input in the reconciliation setup screen; the statement ending balance and date are required.
explanations.b: Routing and account numbers are used when setting up bank feed connectivity, not when beginning a reconciliation.
explanations.c: The previous reconciliation date is displayed by QBO automatically; the bookkeeper does not re-enter it in the setup screen.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states the bookkeeper enters the statement ending balance and the statement ending date from the bank statement when initiating a new reconciliation in QBO.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.11 Reconciliation — C vs. R status markers
questions.keyword: C cleared current reconciliation R reconciled prior period
questions.text: During a bank reconciliation in QuickBooks Online, cleared transactions are marked with status letters. What do C and R represent in the reconciliation transaction list?

answers.text: C means the transaction was checked as cleared during the current reconciliation session; R means it was reconciled in a prior completed reconciliation.
C means the transaction is in the Reviewed bank feed tab; R means it was manually added and then reconciled.
C stands for Credited (deposits) and R stands for Received (checks) to indicate transaction flow direction.
C means the transaction is uncleared and needs review; R means it is ready to be reconciled this period.

explanations.a: The Student Guide explains that C indicates a transaction has been checked (cleared) during the current reconciliation session, while R indicates the transaction was reconciled in a previously completed reconciliation period.
explanations.b: The bank feed Reviewed tab status is separate from reconciliation status markers; C and R relate to reconciliation, not bank feed tabs.
explanations.c: C and R in reconciliation refer to cleared status (current session vs prior period), not to the direction of cash flow.
explanations.d: This interpretation reverses the correct meaning; C represents cleared (checked in the current session) and R represents previously reconciled, not uncleared.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: Save for later reconciliation preserve checkmarks resume later
questions.text: A bookkeeper is partway through a reconciliation when an urgent situation requires them to stop. What should they do to preserve their work and return to finish later?

answers.text: Click Finish now, which saves the current state even if the Difference is not yet zero.
Click Save for later, which preserves the checkmarks placed on cleared transactions so work can resume where it left off.
Print a screenshot of the reconciliation screen and manually re-enter the checkmarks when returning.
Close the browser tab; QBO auto-saves reconciliation progress without any action required.

explanations.a: Finish now requires the Difference to be $0.00; clicking it with a non-zero Difference does not save the session, it would create an unbalanced reconciliation or prompt for a correcting entry.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states bookkeepers can click Save for later during a reconciliation to preserve all checkmarks placed so far, allowing them to return and complete the reconciliation at a later time.
explanations.c: QBO provides a Save for later button specifically for this purpose; manual note-taking is unnecessary.
explanations.d: QBO does not automatically save reconciliation progress when the browser tab is closed; the Save for later button must be explicitly clicked.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: Exclude personal transaction not business Excluded tab
questions.text: A personal charge mistakenly made on a business bank account appears in the Banking Center For Review tab and should not be posted to the company's books. What is the appropriate Banking Center action?

answers.text: Click Add and code it to an Owner's Draw equity account to properly record it.
Click Match and link it to an existing Owner's Draw journal entry in QBO.
Click Exclude to move the transaction to the Excluded tab, preventing it from posting to the books.
Delete the transaction from the bank download file and re-upload the corrected file.

explanations.a: Clicking Add and coding to Owner's Draw does post the transaction to QBO; Exclude is the correct choice when the transaction should not appear in the books at all.
explanations.b: Matching to a journal entry still records the transaction in QBO; the Exclude action is needed to prevent any posting.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that transactions which should not post to the company's books — such as personal charges on a business account — should be moved to the Excluded tab using the Exclude action.
explanations.d: Re-uploading a modified download file is not a supported or necessary workflow in QBO; the Exclude feature handles this directly within the Banking Center.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: Undo Reviewed tab accidentally accepted return For Review
questions.text: A bookkeeper accidentally accepted a bank feed transaction that was already entered manually in QBO, creating a duplicate. Where and how can this acceptance be undone?

answers.text: In the For Review tab, click the transaction and select Unmatch to return it to For Review.
In the Chart of Accounts, find the duplicated transaction and click Undo next to its entry.
In the Audit Log, find the bank feed acceptance event and select Undo to reverse the action.
In the Reviewed tab, find the accepted transaction and click Undo to return it to the For Review tab.

explanations.a: Once a transaction is accepted, it is no longer in the For Review tab; the Undo must be performed from the Reviewed tab.
explanations.b: The Chart of Accounts does not provide an Undo action next to individual transactions; Undo for bank feed actions is in the Reviewed tab.
explanations.c: The Audit Log is a read-only record of changes; it does not have an Undo function for bank feed acceptances.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that to undo an accepted or matched bank feed transaction, the bookkeeper goes to the Reviewed tab, finds the transaction, and clicks Undo to return it to the For Review tab.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.7 Bank rules — conditions and action structure
questions.keyword: bank rule conditions description contains action assign account payee
questions.text: When creating a bank rule in QuickBooks Online, the bookkeeper configures conditions and an action. Which description correctly explains the structure of a bank rule?

answers.text: The bookkeeper sets conditions (such as the transaction description contains a specific word) and an action (such as categorize to a specific account and assign a payee), which QBO applies to future qualifying downloaded transactions.
Bank rules define a scheduling interval for automatic bank feed updates and the account to receive all downloaded transactions.
Bank rules set a dollar threshold above which downloaded transactions are automatically moved to the Excluded tab for manual review.
Bank rules create recurring journal entries that post automatically each time a matching bank transaction is downloaded.

explanations.a: The Student Guide describes bank rules as having conditions (such as the bank text or description containing specific words) and actions (such as assigning a payee and account category), which QBO applies automatically to qualifying future downloaded transactions.
explanations.b: Bank feed scheduling is separate from bank rules; rules act on transactions after they have been downloaded, not on the download schedule itself.
explanations.c: Setting a dollar threshold to route transactions to the Excluded tab is not a bank rule function described in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Bank rules assign categories to bank feed transactions; they do not create recurring journal entries.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: batch actions select multiple transactions accept Banking Center
questions.text: Multiple downloaded transactions waiting in the Banking Center can be processed simultaneously using batch actions. Which batch action is available for transactions in the For Review tab?

answers.text: Match All — QBO automatically matches every For Review transaction to the nearest existing QBO record.
Accept Selected — the bookkeeper selects multiple transactions and accepts them all at once using the batch action drop-down.
Categorize All — QBO assigns every For Review transaction to the most recently used account.
Exclude All — removes all For Review transactions from the banking feed without posting any of them.

explanations.a: Match All is not a described batch action in the Student Guide; QBO does not force-match every transaction without bookkeeper review.
explanations.b: The Student Guide describes the ability to select multiple transactions using checkboxes in the For Review tab and then use a batch action such as Accept to process them all at once.
explanations.c: Categorize All is not a batch action described in the Student Guide; the bookkeeper must individually review account assignments or use rules.
explanations.d: Exclude All is not a described batch action; excluding would remove transactions that may need to be posted, which would not be appropriate as a blanket action.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: white 2 records found multiple potential matches bookkeeper choose
questions.text: A downloaded bank transaction displays a white indicator reading '2 records found' in the For Review tab. What does this indicate?

answers.text: The bank download file contained two identical transactions that must be merged before the bookkeeper can proceed.
Two bank rules match this transaction, and QBO is asking the bookkeeper to choose which rule to apply.
QBO found two existing QBO transactions that could be a potential match, and the bookkeeper must select the correct one.
The transaction was previously accepted and then undone, creating two versions of the record in QBO.

explanations.a: The number in the indicator reflects possible matching QBO transactions, not duplicate entries in the download file.
explanations.b: A white indicator with a count refers to potential transaction matches, not to competing bank rules.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states a white '2 records found' indicator means QBO identified two existing QBO transactions that could potentially match the downloaded entry; the bookkeeper must open the match options and select the correct one.
explanations.d: A previously undone transaction returns to For Review; the white indicator reflects multiple potential matches rather than version history.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: beginning balance discrepancy edited deleted reconciled transaction
questions.text: A bookkeeper starts a new reconciliation in QuickBooks Online and finds that the beginning balance shown by QBO does not match the opening balance on the current bank statement. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: The wrong bank account was selected when initiating the reconciliation.
The statement ending date entered in the previous reconciliation was incorrect.
The bank changed the account number since the last reconciliation, resetting the balance.
A previously reconciled transaction was edited or deleted after the prior reconciliation was completed, altering the cleared balance.

explanations.a: Selecting the wrong account would result in a completely wrong set of transactions, not just an off beginning balance; the more common cause is an edited or deleted reconciled transaction.
explanations.b: An incorrect ending date in a prior reconciliation is possible but not the most common cause described in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: A bank account number change does not automatically reset the QBO beginning balance; data continuity is maintained unless the account is deleted and re-added.
explanations.d: The Student Guide identifies editing or deleting a previously reconciled transaction as the most common cause of a beginning balance discrepancy, because QBO's cleared balance is recalculated when reconciled transactions are modified.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.1 Bank feeds — connecting an account automatically
questions.keyword: bank feeds connect name online banking credentials automatic
questions.text: When linking a bank account to QuickBooks Online using the automatic bank feed connection, what does the bookkeeper typically need to provide?

answers.text: The bank's name (searched in QBO) and then the same online banking credentials used to log into the bank's website.
The bank's routing number, account number, and a one-time verification PIN mailed by the bank.
A QBO administrator token from Intuit Customer Support and the bank's API key.
A notarized letter of authorization, the bank account number, and the company's EIN.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states the bookkeeper searches for the bank by name in QBO's bank connection tool and then enters the same online banking credentials used to access the bank's website to establish the automatic feed connection.
explanations.b: A mailed verification PIN is not the standard automatic bank feed connection process described in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: Administrator tokens and API keys are not the credentials described for standard bank feed setup in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Notarized letters and EINs are not required for automatic bank feed connections as described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: reconciliation report summary detail Finish now
questions.text: After clicking Finish now with a $0.00 Difference, what does QuickBooks Online produce?

answers.text: A Bank Feed Summary report listing every transaction downloaded during the reconciled period.
A Reconciliation report — including a Reconciliation Summary and Reconciliation Detail — that can be viewed or printed.
A Bank Statement Audit report automatically emailed to the company admin and the connected accountant.
A Journal Entry Summary report listing all journal entries posted as part of the reconciliation.

explanations.a: A Bank Feed Summary report is not a report produced at the end of reconciliation in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that after a reconciliation is completed, QBO produces a Reconciliation report including a Summary and a Detail version, which can be viewed and printed.
explanations.c: QBO does not automatically email a Bank Statement Audit report to admins or accountants when a reconciliation is finalized.
explanations.d: Reconciliation does not produce a Journal Entry Summary; it produces a Reconciliation report. A correcting journal entry would only appear if QBO created one to resolve a discrepancy.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: bank rules priority order list reorder bookkeeper
questions.text: When multiple bank rules could apply to the same downloaded transaction in QuickBooks Online, how does QBO determine which rule to use?

answers.text: QBO applies all matching rules simultaneously, combining the category assignments from each rule.
QBO applies the most recently created rule first, then checks older rules if no match is confirmed.
QBO applies the rule with the highest priority, determined by the rule's position in the bank rules list, which the bookkeeper can reorder.
QBO applies the rule with the most specific conditions first, regardless of position in the rules list.

explanations.a: QBO does not apply multiple rules simultaneously; only one rule is applied, based on priority order.
explanations.b: The Student Guide does not describe a creation-date priority for bank rules; position in the rules list determines priority.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states bank rules are applied based on their priority order in the rules list, and the bookkeeper can reorder them to control which rule takes precedence when multiple rules match a transaction.
explanations.d: While specificity is a logical tiebreaker concept, the Student Guide describes rule order in the list as the controlling factor for priority.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: credit card reconciliation same Reconcile feature liability balance
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to reconcile a company credit card account in QuickBooks Online. Which statement about credit card reconciliation is accurate?

answers.text: Credit card accounts cannot be reconciled in QBO; only bank accounts support the Reconcile feature.
Credit card reconciliation uses a separate CC Reconcile tool accessed from the Banking Center, not from the Accounting tab.
When reconciling a credit card, the statement ending balance represents the available credit remaining on the card.
Credit card accounts can be reconciled using the same Reconcile feature as bank accounts; the statement ending balance represents the amount owed on the card.

explanations.a: The QBO Reconcile feature supports both bank accounts and credit card accounts; credit cards can be reconciled in the same way.
explanations.b: There is no separate CC Reconcile tool; the standard Accounting → Reconcile path handles credit card accounts.
explanations.c: The statement ending balance for a credit card reconciliation represents the amount owed (the balance due on the card), not the available credit remaining.
explanations.d: The Student Guide indicates that credit card accounts are reconciled using the same Reconcile feature; the key difference is that the statement ending balance represents the amount owed on the credit card, which is a liability balance.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: reconciliation Difference not zero add missing transaction bank service charge
questions.text: After clearing all transactions, a bookkeeper's reconciliation shows a Difference of -$15 caused by a bank service charge that was never entered in QBO. What is the correct way to resolve this?

answers.text: Enter the bank service charge as a new transaction in QBO (or add it directly during reconciliation), check it as cleared, and confirm the Difference returns to $0.00 before clicking Finish now.
Click Finish now with the -$15 Difference; QBO creates an automatic adjusting journal entry to bring the balance to zero.
Click the -$15 Difference amount to trigger a bank error report that Intuit submits to the financial institution.
Close the reconciliation without finishing and contact the bank to reverse the service charge before attempting again.

explanations.a: The Student Guide indicates that when the Difference is non-zero due to a missing transaction, the bookkeeper should create the missing transaction in QBO, check it as cleared in the reconciliation, and verify the Difference reaches $0.00 before clicking Finish now.
explanations.b: While QBO can create an adjusting entry when Finish now is clicked with a non-zero Difference, best practice is to identify and enter the missing transaction so the reconciliation is accurate rather than relying on an automatic entry.
explanations.c: Clicking the Difference amount does not trigger a bank error report; it is simply a calculated display field.
explanations.d: Closing without finishing and contacting the bank for a $15 service charge reversal is not the approach the Student Guide recommends; the charge should be entered in QBO.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: .QBO QuickBooks Web Connect native format financial institution
questions.text: When downloading bank transaction files from a financial institution's website for import into QuickBooks Online, which file format is the native QuickBooks format specifically designed for QuickBooks products?

answers.text: .CSV, which is the universal format accepted by all financial software including QBO.
.QBO, which is the QuickBooks Web Connect format designed specifically for import into QuickBooks products.
.QFX (Quicken Financial Exchange), which is the same format used internally by QuickBooks Online.
.OFX (Open Financial Exchange), the original standard format that QBO and all QuickBooks products prefer.

explanations.a: .CSV is a widely accepted format that QBO supports, but it is not the native QuickBooks-specific format.
explanations.b: The Student Guide identifies .QBO (QuickBooks Web Connect) as the native format designed specifically for QuickBooks product imports; banks that support QuickBooks directly offer .QBO downloads.
explanations.c: .QFX is the Quicken Financial Exchange format used by Quicken software; it is similar to .QBO but is not the QuickBooks-native format.
explanations.d: .OFX is the Open Financial Exchange standard from which both .QBO and .QFX were derived; it is supported but is not described as QBO's preferred or native format.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.13 Reconciliation — effect of modifying a reconciled transaction
questions.keyword: modified reconciled transaction uncleared beginning balance discrepancy next period
questions.text: A bookkeeper edits a transaction that was cleared and reconciled in a prior period — changing its dollar amount. What does QuickBooks Online do, and what problem results?

answers.text: QBO prevents the change by locking all previously reconciled transactions automatically.
QBO allows the change and sends an automated email alert to the company admin noting the modification.
QBO allows the change but marks the transaction as uncleared, causing the beginning balance of the next reconciliation to differ from the prior period's ending balance by the changed amount.
QBO automatically reverses the transaction and creates a correcting journal entry dated the first day of the following period.

explanations.a: QBO does not automatically lock reconciled transactions; they can be edited (unless a closing date password is used), which is exactly why this is a common reconciliation issue.
explanations.b: QBO does not automatically send email alerts when reconciled transactions are modified; the discrepancy typically surfaces at the next reconciliation.
explanations.c: The Student Guide explains that editing a previously reconciled transaction causes QBO to treat it as uncleared, which shifts the beginning balance of the next reconciliation period, creating a discrepancy that must be investigated.
explanations.d: QBO does not automatically reverse modified reconciled transactions or create correcting journal entries; the bookkeeper must identify and resolve the discrepancy manually.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.7 Bank rules — Auto-add vs. Auto-match final actions
questions.keyword: bank rule Auto-add post directly Auto-match existing QBO transaction
questions.text: After configuring conditions for a bank rule in QuickBooks Online, the bookkeeper selects a final action for qualifying transactions. Which action does a bank rule perform on matched transactions by default when the rule fires?

answers.text: Auto-categorize and Auto-exclude.
Auto-reconcile and Auto-accept.
Auto-split and Auto-merge.
Auto-add (post the transaction directly to QBO books) and Auto-match (automatically match it to an existing QBO transaction).

explanations.a: Auto-exclude is not a final action for bank rules; Auto-categorize is part of the rule setup but the two final action choices are Auto-add and Auto-match.
explanations.b: Auto-reconcile is not a bank rule action; Auto-accept is a general term but the specific options described in QBO are Auto-add and Auto-match.
explanations.c: Auto-split and Auto-merge are not bank rule final action options described in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: The Student Guide describes two possible final actions for a bank rule: Auto-add, which posts the transaction directly to QBO as a new record, and Auto-match, which automatically matches the downloaded transaction to an existing QBO transaction.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.keyword: beginning balance zero bank account no opening balance entry
questions.text: A company that has never reconciled in QBO finds the beginning balance shown on the reconciliation screen is $0 rather than the actual bank balance. What is the likely cause?

answers.text: The bank account was set up in QBO without an opening balance entry; the bookkeeper must enter the correct opening balance through the Chart of Accounts or a journal entry, then reconcile all historical periods to establish an accurate cleared balance.
The bank account was connected to the wrong routing number; the bookkeeper must disconnect and reconnect the bank feed with the correct credentials.
The Reconcile feature requires at least three months of bank feed data before QBO calculates a beginning balance.
Advanced subscription is required for QBO to display a beginning balance in the reconciliation screen.

explanations.a: The Student Guide and standard QBO practice indicate that if a bank account was added to QBO without an opening balance, the reconciliation beginning balance will be $0; the resolution is to enter the correct opening balance via the Chart of Accounts and then reconcile all unreconciled periods.
explanations.b: A wrong routing number affects bank feed connectivity, not the reconciliation beginning balance derived from QBO's own transaction records.
explanations.c: The reconciliation beginning balance is calculated from QBO's cleared transactions, not from the quantity of bank feed data; three months of data is not a prerequisite.
explanations.d: Reconciliation is available at all QBO subscription levels; Advanced is not required for the feature or for the beginning balance to appear.

questions.name: Banking, Feeds & Reconciliation
questions.objective: 7.1 Bank feeds — manual file upload for non-connected banks
questions.keyword: manual upload .CSV .QFX credit union not automatic feed
questions.text: A company's credit union does not support automatic bank feeds with QuickBooks Online. According to the Student Guide, how can the bookkeeper still get transactions into the Banking Center?

answers.text: Transactions must be entered manually in QBO one by one; there is no import option for non-connected banks.
The bookkeeper downloads a transaction file in a supported format (.CSV, .QFX, .QBO, or .OFX) from the credit union's online portal and manually uploads it into QBO's Banking Center.
The bookkeeper must contact Intuit to request a custom bank feed connection for the credit union, which typically takes 30 to 60 business days.
The bookkeeper enters the credit union's online banking credentials in QBO, which then scrapes transactions automatically without an official connection.

explanations.a: Manual one-by-one entry is not the only option for non-connected banks; the Student Guide describes the file upload method as an alternative.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that for banks not supporting automatic feeds, the bookkeeper can download a transaction file in one of the supported formats (.CSV, .QFX, .QBO, or .OFX) from the bank's online portal and upload it manually into the QBO Banking Center.
explanations.c: Contacting Intuit to build a custom connection is not described as the standard solution for non-connected institutions; file upload is the recommended alternative.
explanations.d: QBO's Banking Center does not include a credential-scraping feature; transactions must come through an official feed or a manually uploaded file.
